title: The Ito Integral with Respect to Brownian Motion

items.title: Continuous-time adapted processes and martingales
items.statement: Assume AC. On a filtered probability space, X is adapted when X_t is F_t-measurable; it is a martingale when integrable and E[X_t|F_s]=X_s for s<=t, and a local martingale when stopping times tau_n increase to infinity almost surely and each X^{tau_n}-X_0 is a martingale. Continuous, square-integrable and L2-bounded have their usual path and integrability meanings.
items.strategy: Reconcile the all-pairs supplier with process notation, verify deterministic times are stopping times, and record localization of X-X_0 explicitly.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Sections 4.1 and 5.4

items.title: Progressively measurable and predictable processes
items.statement: H is progressively measurable if its restriction to [0,t] times Omega is B([0,t]) tensor F_t measurable for every t. The predictable sigma-algebra is generated by (s,t] times A, A in F_s, and {0} times A, A in F_0; H is predictable when measurable for it.
items.strategy: Check the generator and time-zero convention; derive deterministic-time adaptedness and finite-horizon product measurability.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.1

items.title: Adapted continuous processes are progressively measurable
items.statement: Every real process with F_t-measurable sections and everywhere continuous paths is progressively measurable and predictable, including time zero; normalization off a full-probability F_0 event is allowed.
items.strategy: On each [0,T], approximate at positive time by left-endpoint dyadic steps. These are predictable and product measurable; path continuity gives pointwise convergence on (0,T]. At time zero use the F_0-measurable section on the generator {0} times F_0. Pointwise-limit measurability closes both claims. The measurable-section hypothesis is explicit; no conditional-expectation interface is imported.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.1

items.title: Elementary predictable Brownian integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix Brownian motion B on a filtered probability space with respect to which B is Brownian, in particular the usual augmented natural Brownian filtration used below. On [0,T], an elementary predictable integrand is H_s=sum xi_k 1_(t_k,t_{k+1}](s), where 0=t_0<...<t_m=T and bounded xi_k is F_{t_k}-measurable; endpoint values are immaterial modulo dt tensor P.
items.strategy: Verify predictability from the generating rectangles, square integrability from boundedness, and endpoint irrelevance from Lebesgue-null finite sets.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Ito integral of an elementary predictable process
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary H define I_t(H)=sum xi_k(B_{t wedge t_{k+1}}-B_{t wedge t_k}) and write it as integral_0^t H_s dB_s.
items.strategy: Define the finite sum on the common Brownian continuity event and check adaptedness and continuity termwise.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Elementary Ito integrals do not depend on step representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Two elementary representations equal dt tensor P almost everywhere have almost surely equal terminal Ito sums; deterministic partition refinement changes nothing.
items.strategy: Use a common refinement. For their difference expand the expected squared sum; conditional centering kills cross terms and Brownian variance turns diagonal terms into its product-L2 energy, which is zero by Tonelli.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.20 and Lemma 5.22

items.title: Ito isometry for elementary integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary predictable H, I_t(H) is a continuous square-integrable martingale and E[I_t(H)^2]=E integral_0^t H_s^2 ds.
items.strategy: Refine to include s,t. Conditional centering proves the martingale identity. Expanding the square kills cross terms and evaluates each diagonal term as E[xi_k^2]Delta t_k; continuity is pathwise.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.1

items.title: Cross Ito isometry
items.statement: Assume AC. For elementary predictable H,K, E[I_t(H)I_t(K)]=E integral_0^t H_sK_s ds.
items.strategy: Apply the isometry to H+K, subtract the identities for H and K, and expand both squares.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.22

items.title: Density of elementary predictable processes in predictable L2
items.statement: Assume AC. On every finite horizon, bounded elementary predictable processes are dense in predictable L2(dt tensor P), modulo product-almost-everywhere equality.
items.strategy: Predictable generating rectangles have elementary indicators and form a pi-system containing the whole finite product (with the time-zero generator harmless modulo dt tensor P). Let D be the predictable sets whose indicators are L2-limits of bounded elementary processes. D contains that pi-system, is closed under complements, and is closed under countable disjoint unions: finite partial unions remain elementary-approximable, and dominated convergence sends their indicators to the union in L2. Thus D is a lambda-system; Dynkin pi-lambda gives every predictable set. Finite simple approximation, truncation, and Riesz-Fischer then give density for arbitrary predictable L2 classes.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemmas 5.21-5.23

items.title: Ito integral for square-integrable predictable processes
items.statement: Assume AC. For predictable H in L2([0,T] times Omega), choose elementary H^n converging in predictable L2 and define integral_0^T H_s dB_s as the L2(Omega) limit of I_T(H^n); at t use 1_[0,t]H.
items.strategy: Density supplies an approximation, the isometry makes its images Cauchy, and Riesz-Fischer supplies their L2 limit. Keep domain and range as a.e. quotient classes.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25

items.title: The general Ito integral is well defined
items.statement: Assume AC. The L2 Ito integral is independent of elementary approximation and of the predictable dt tensor P representative.
items.strategy: Interlace two approximations; isometry makes the distance of image limits equal the vanishing domain distance. Product-a.e.-equal representatives have distance zero.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25 and Theorem 5.26

items.title: Ito isometry and linearity in predictable L2
items.statement: Assume AC. H maps linearly and isometrically to integral_0^t H dB in mean-zero L2(Omega), and E[(integral H dB)(integral K dB)]=E integral HK ds.
items.strategy: Approximate H,K simultaneously; pass elementary linearity and the cross identity through L2 limits, using Cauchy-Schwarz for products. L2 limits preserve zero expectation.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Sections 3.2.2-3.2.3

items.title: The Ito integral process has a continuous martingale version
items.statement: Assume AC. If H is predictable and square-integrable on finite horizons, M_t=integral_0^t H_s dB_s has an adapted continuous square-integrable-martingale version, unique up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Use AC to select elementary representations at summable L2 tolerances and integer horizons. Countable-grid Doob bounds give uniform convergence on a measurable probability-one event. Define the finite limsup, zero otherwise, separately at each time to preserve adaptedness without completing the filtration. Fixed-time L2 convergence passes martingale identities. Glue integer horizons and use rational equality plus continuity for uniqueness on a measurable full-probability event.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.26
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.4

items.title: Doob maximal bound for the Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. E sup_{t<=T}|integral_0^t H_s dB_s|^2 <=4 E integral_0^T H_s^2 ds for predictable square-integrable H.
items.strategy: Apply discrete Doob L2 on increasing rational grids. Continuity and monotone convergence pass grid maxima to the path supremum, then terminal isometry gives the bound.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Proposition 3.2.4

items.title: Locally square-integrable predictable Brownian integrands
items.statement: Assume AC. Predictable H is locally square-integrable when integral_0^t H_s^2ds is finite almost surely for every finite t. Set tau_n=inf{t:integral_0^t H_s^2ds>=n} wedge n.
items.strategy: Tonelli gives measurable accumulated energy; its continuous adapted paths show tau_n is a stopping time. Local finiteness makes tau_n increase to infinity almost surely.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Sections 5.4-5.5

items.title: Localized Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. Every locally square-integrable predictable H has a continuous local-martingale integral H dot B, characterized by its stopped square-integrable integrals and independent of the localizing sequence up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Construct finite-energy stopped integrals. Isometry proves agreement on overlaps; continuity upgrades rational-time equality to indistinguishability. Patch them, then compare pairwise minima for any second localization. The stopped pieces prove the local-martingale property. First construct progressive versions by left dyadic samples; finite normalized limits and measurable stopped evaluations avoid raw-filtration null-set issues. Use almost-sure locally finite energy under the supplier's usual conditions and positive localization indices; completeness makes the exceptional-path hitting-time discrepancies measurable.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.33 and Theorem 5.36

items.title: Stopping an Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. For a stopping time tau and locally square-integrable predictable H, (H dot B)_{t wedge tau}=integral_0^t 1_{s<=tau}H_s dB_s up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Apply the already proved finite-energy stopping identity on the original positive-index canonical energy intervals. For G=H1_[0,tau], those stopping times exhaust almost surely under the usual conditions and bound the stopped expected energy. Progressive stopped evaluation gives adapted N; the localization characterization identifies N with G dot B.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.28 and Theorem 5.36

items.title: Quadratic variation of an Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. If M=H dot B, then along every deterministic partition sequence with mesh tending to zero, squared-increment partial sums converge uniformly in probability on [0,T] to [M]_t=integral_0^t H_s^2ds.
items.strategy: For arbitrary deterministic Brownian partitions, centered squared increments form a discrete martingale with variance at most 2T times mesh; Doob and continuity give uniform convergence. Prove the claim blockwise for elementary H. For L2 limits, Cauchy-Schwarz bounds differences of square sums by the product of sum-squares for M-M^n and M+M^n; isometry controls them. Finish by energy localization. Correct zero partial sum and deterministic boundary-refinement bound; uniform expected approximation errors and epsilon split, then almost-sure energy localization under usual conditions, with energy normalized on its F_0 null exceptional event. No general almost-sure dyadic claim.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.8 and Lemma 5.77
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Theorem 3.2.6

items.title: Deterministic Ito integrals are Gaussian
items.statement: Assume AC. For deterministic h in L2[0,T], integral h dB is centered normal with variance integral h^2. Finite families are jointly Gaussian with covariance integral hk.
items.strategy: Use published box-step density on the zero extension of h to R, restrict the approximants to [0,T], and refine their finitely many endpoints to deterministic elementary step functions. Their integrals are linear combinations of independent Gaussian increments; isometry gives convergence in probability and the variances converge. Characteristic functions identify the limit law, including zero variance. Apply the same argument to every scalar linear combination of a finite family and use the stated projection definition; cross isometry yields the covariance integral.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2 and Exercise 3.8

title: The Ito Integral with Respect to Brownian Motion — Examples

items.title: A deterministic step integrand
items.statement: Assume AC. For h=sum a_k 1_(t_k,t_{k+1}], its Ito integral is sum a_k(B_{t wedge t_{k+1}}-B_{t wedge t_k}) and at T is N(0,sum a_k^2 Delta t_k).
items.strategy: Substitute into the elementary definition and evaluate the step function's L2 norm in the Gaussian corollary.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Indicator of a stopping interval
items.statement: Assume AC. For every stopping time tau, integral_0^t 1_{s<=tau}dB_s=B_{t wedge tau}-B_0 up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Apply stopping to H=1, whose elementary integral is B_t-B_0.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.3

items.title: Covariance of deterministic Ito integrals
items.statement: Assume AC. For deterministic h,k in L2[0,T], Cov(integral h dB,integral k dB)=integral hk; disjoint supports therefore give independent integrals.
items.strategy: Use cross isometry; joint Gaussianity turns zero covariance into independence.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Lemma 5.22

items.title: Integral of Brownian motion against itself
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). Use the explicitly constructed predictable Brownian representative beta. Integral beta dB=(B_t^2-t)/2 on a common full event for the continuous integral version; mean zero, variance t^2/2, non-Gaussian for t>0.
items.strategy: Construct beta by predictable left-grid finite limits. Prove L2 step approximation and coefficient truncation; telescope squares and use terminal dyadic QV plus Fatou to identify the limit. Rational times and continuity give the process identity. No later Ito formula.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, equation (3.8)

items.title: A deterministic time-changed quadratic variation
items.statement: Assume AC. For M_t=integral_0^t s dB_s, [M]_t=t^3/3.
items.strategy: Apply the quadratic-variation theorem to H_s=s and integrate s squared.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Theorem 3.2.6

items.title: A nonadapted step integrand breaks the Ito isometry
items.statement: Assume AC. For T>0, naively taking H_s=1_{|B_T|>sqrt(T)} on (0,T] gives E[H^2B_T^2]>T E[H^2], contrary to Ito isometry; H is not F_0-measurable.
items.strategy: On A={|B_T|>sqrt(T)}, B_T^2>T and P(A)>0 from the normal density. The strict expectation inequality follows and the terminal coefficient violates predictability.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.2.2

items.title: Bounded-variation Riemann-Stieltjes theory does not construct the Brownian Ito integral
items.statement: Assume AC. Almost surely Brownian paths have infinite total variation on every nondegenerate compact interval, so the classical bounded-variation construction of integral f dg for every continuous f cannot define Brownian Ito integration pathwise.
items.strategy: Apply the Brownian infinite-variation corollary. Claim only failure of the bounded-variation construction, not nonexistence of every special pathwise integral.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 2.8

items.title: Product-measure equality is not pointwise equality
items.statement: Assume AC. H(t,omega)=1_{t=1/2} and K=0 are deterministic predictable processes equal dt tensor P almost everywhere, but as raw processes they differ exactly on {1/2} times Omega (only their t=1/2 sections differ); their Ito integrals agree.
items.strategy: The singleton {1/2} is Lebesgue null and its deterministic indicator is predictable. General-integral well-definedness identifies the product-a.e. classes despite the explicitly isolated raw pointwise discrepancy.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.25

items.title: Continuous Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. A real continuous Brownian Ito process is X_t=X_0+integral_0^t b_s ds+integral_0^t sigma_s dB_s, where X_0 is finite and F_0-measurable, b is real progressively measurable with integral_0^t |b_s|ds finite a.s., and sigma is real predictable with integral_0^t sigma_s^2ds finite a.s. for every finite t. In dimension d driven by m-dimensional Brownian motion, X_0 is finite F_0-measurable in R^d, b takes values in R^d, and sigma takes values in R^{d times m}, with the same componentwise local integrability conditions. Use progressive process representatives and almost-sure locally integrable drift/energy coefficients under the usual conditions; indistinguishability means agreement on a measurable full event.
items.strategy: Use pathwise Lebesgue integration for b and the localized Ito integral for each row of sigma; finite componentwise sums give continuity and adaptedness. The displayed dimensions prevent an untyped matrix convention.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.9

items.title: Quadratic covariation of Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: For continuous X,Y, [X,Y] is a single continuous process such that, for every deterministic partition sequence whose mesh tends to zero, the paired-increment partial-sum processes converge to it uniformly in probability on every compact time interval; when such a common limit exists write [X]=[X,X].
items.strategy: Specify the stopped partial-sum convention and require the same UCP limit for every deterministic vanishing-mesh sequence, rather than a sequence-dependent value. Record polarization 4[X,Y]=[X+Y]-[X-Y] whenever these common quadratic variations exist. Require fixed-time random variables and continuous candidate limits; normalize on measurable continuity events and use rational suprema for measurable uniform errors and uniqueness.
items.axiom_base: ZF

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Definition 5.62 and Theorem 5.64

items.title: Quadratic covariation of Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. If dX^i=b^idt+sum_k sigma^{ik}dB^k, then [X^i,X^j]_t=sum_k integral_0^t sigma_s^{ik}sigma_s^{jk}ds; continuous finite-variation parts have zero covariation with continuous Ito martingale parts.
items.strategy: For terms driven by the same Brownian coordinate, polarize the scalar quadratic-variation theorem. For distinct coordinates, prove the elementary cross-increment sums converge to zero by conditional centering and an L2 mesh bound, then pass through predictable-L2 approximation and localization. Bound finite-variation cross sums by maximum martingale increment times total variation, which vanishes after localization by continuity. Use vector increments independent of the full past on a refined grid, explicit oscillation error, both finite-energy approximation terms and common pairwise energy stopping times; zero drift does not imply zero bracket. Use usual conditions and normalize all coefficient path integrals on the common full event of local integrability.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Section 5.8

items.title: Integration by parts for Brownian Ito processes
items.statement: Assume AC. For continuous Brownian Ito processes X,Y, X_tY_t=X_0Y_0+integral X_sdY_s+integral Y_sdX_s+[X,Y]_t, with differential integrals expanded into Lebesgue and Ito parts.
items.strategy: Normalize X,Y and coefficients simultaneously on a common F0 full event under the usual conditions. Local compact bounds make all drift and diffusion products integrable. Apply scalar Ito to z² for X,Y and X+Y; subtract and divide by two. Common energy stops justify localized linearity. Identify the cross coefficient with covariation. In the zero-drift case prove the local-martingale assertion under the initial-value convention; finite energy and the two additional L1 assumptions license each expectation.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, equation (5.63)

items.title: One-dimensional Ito formula
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X be a real continuous Brownian Ito process dX_t=b_tdt+sigma_tdB_t and let f belong to C^{1,2}([0,infinity) times R). Then, up to indistinguishability, for every t>=0, f(t,X_t)=f(0,X_0)+integral_0^t (f_t+b f_x+(sigma^2/2)f_xx)(s,X_s)ds+integral_0^t sigma_s f_x(s,X_s)dB_s, with all terms defined after the standard localizations.
items.strategy: First prove the formula for C^3 functions after stopping X, integral |b|, and integral sigma^2 inside deterministic compact bounds. Apply third-order Taylor on deterministic partitions; the first-order terms converge to the Lebesgue and Ito integrals, the quadratic term uses the already proved covariation theorem, and mixed, time-square, and cubic remainders vanish locally uniformly in probability by continuity, Cauchy-Schwarz, and maximal-mesh control. For f in C^{1,2}, choose a compact space-time cylinder strictly containing the stopped path range, multiply by a cutoff, extend across t=0 by the explicit C1 reflection 2f(0,x)-f(-t,x), and convolve with an explicit smooth product mollifier. On the smaller cylinder f_n, partial_t f_n, partial_x f_n, and partial_xx f_n converge uniformly to the corresponding derivatives. Apply the C^3 case and pass the drift terms by dominated convergence and the stochastic terms by Ito isometry plus the maximal bound. Then remove the localization. This is the binding C^3-first, localization-and-mollification route. Normalize on the F_0 null event first. Use separate X and M quadratic sums, an explicit tightness cutoff for weighted convergence, absolute remainder bounds, and eventual rho_c=T to remove localization. Mollify the continuous cutoff on nested cylinders before smoothing f.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.79
Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.3

items.title: Multidimensional Ito formula for Brownian-driven processes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $m,d\ge1$ be finite
integers, let $B=(B^1,\dots,B^m)$ be a standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion,
and let $X$ be an $\mathbb R^d$-valued continuous Brownian Ito process
$$X^i_t=X^i_0+\int_0^tb^i_s\,ds+\sum_{k=1}^m\int_0^t\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s, \qquad i=1,\dots,d,$$
in the sense of [[def-continuous-brownian-ito-process]], including its usual-filtration and almost-sure coefficient-integrability conventions. Let
$f\in C^{1,2}([0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d)$, meaning that $f,\partial_tf$,
$\partial_if$ and $\partial_i\partial_jf$ ($1\le i,j\le d$) exist and are
continuous. Then, up to indistinguishability, for every $t\ge0$
$$f(t,X_t)=f(0,X_0)+\int_0^t\Bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\Bigr)(s,X_s)\,ds+\sum_{i,k}\int_0^t\partial_if(s,X_s)\sigma^{ik}_s\,dB^k_s,$$
For the displayed integrands, intersect the measurable full events of continuity and the decomposition of $X$, and of coefficient integrability at all integer horizons. Its null complement belongs to $\mathcal F_0$ under the usual conditions. Set $X,X_0,b,\sigma$ to zero there. These representatives preserve all coefficient classes and the decomposition up to indistinguishability, with everywhere continuous $X$ and everywhere locally finite coefficient path integrals. All displayed integrands use these representatives.

The stochastic integrals are localized Ito integrals of the predictable
locally square-integrable integrands $\partial_if(\cdot,X)\sigma^{ik}$, and
$(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}_s=\sum_k\sigma^{ik}_s\sigma^{jk}_s$. In
differential form,
$df(t,X_t)=\bigl(\partial_tf+\sum_ib^i\partial_if+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}(\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T})^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jf\bigr)(t,X_t)\,dt+\sum_{i,k}\partial_if(t,X_t)\sigma^{ik}_t\,dB^k_t$.
items.strategy: Usual conditions and F0 null normalization; initial-value restriction and path/drift/energy stopping; dimension-correct C3 Taylor bound; weighted covariance convergence with explicit tightness split; C1,2 reflection/cutoff/mollifier derivative convergence and countable localization removal.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: van der Vaart, Stochastic Integration and Differential Equations, Theorem 5.79

items.title: The Brownian square martingale
items.statement: Assume AC. B_t^2-t=2 integral_0^t B_sdB_s, hence B_t^2-t is a continuous martingale.
items.strategy: Use f(x)=x^2, b=0, sigma=1. Since E integral_0^T B_s^2ds=T^2/2, the integral is a genuine square-integrable martingale.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, equation (3.8)

items.title: The exponential Brownian martingale
items.statement: Assume AC. For theta real, Z_t=exp(theta B_t-theta^2t/2)=1+theta integral_0^t Z_sdB_s is a positive continuous martingale with E Z_t=1.
items.strategy: Ito cancels the drift. Factor Z_t/Z_s through the independent normal increment; its exponential moment is one, proving the true conditional martingale identity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is stated and declared directly; the implication bridge supplies every inherited DC or AC_omega obligation.

references.title: Lawler, Stochastic Calculus, Section 3.3

items.title: Space-time harmonic functions yield Brownian local martingales up to exit lifetime
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the standing hypothesis (H) of
[[def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand]]. Let $d\ge1$, let
$U\subseteq[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d$ be open in the relative topology, and let
$f\in C^{1,2}(U)$ satisfy the space-time harmonicity equation
$$\partial_tf+\tfrac12\Delta f=0\qquad\text{on }U,$$
where $\Delta=\sum_{k=1}^d\partial^2_{x_k}$ is the spatial Laplacian. Let $B$ be
a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion on a filtration satisfying the usual
conditions, with $(0,0)\in U$. Use its everywhere-continuous adapted representative obtained by setting $B$ to zero off the measurable full event of continuity and $B_0=0$; the usual conditions make that null event $\mathcal F_0$-measurable. This preserves all Brownian laws and the standing increment hypothesis. All exit times and integrands below use this representative. For a compact
$K\subseteq U$ put $\tau_K:=\inf\{t\ge0:(t,B_t)\notin\operatorname{int}K\}$,
where the interior is relative to $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d$.

1. For every compact $K\subseteq U$ with $(0,0)\in\operatorname{int}K$, up to
   indistinguishability
   $$f(t\wedge\tau_K,B_{t\wedge\tau_K})=f(0,0)+\sum_{k=1}^d\int_0^t1_{[0,\tau_K]}(s)\partial_{x_k}f(s,B_s)\,dB^k_s,$$
   and the right-hand integral is a continuous square-integrable martingale;
   thus each stopped piece is a true martingale. In this display the stopped
   gradient is the predictable bounded extension supplied by [F3], equal to
   $\nabla f(s,B_s)$ through $\tau_K$ and zero afterwards; it does not evaluate
   $f$ outside $U$.
2. If $\tau_U:=\inf\{t\ge0:(t,B_t)\notin U\}$ and
   $E\int_0^t|\nabla f|^2(s,B_s)1_{[0,\tau_U)}(s)\,ds<\infty$ for a given
   $t\ge0$, then the process
   $$N_r:=\sum_{k=1}^d\int_0^r1_{[0,\tau_U)}(s)\partial_{x_k}f(s,B_s)\,dB^k_s, \qquad 0\le r\le t,$$
   is a square-integrable martingale, and for every $0\le r\le t$ one has
   $$f(r,B_r)-f(0,0)=N_r\qquad\text{on the event }\{r<\tau_U\}.$$
   No value of $f$ at the exit point $(\tau_U,B_{\tau_U})\notin U$ is asserted.
3. On the stochastic interval $[0,\tau_U)$ the process $t\mapsto f(t,B_t)$,
   read through continuous versions, is a continuous local martingale **up to
   lifetime $\tau_U$**: for any time-capped compact exhaustion satisfying
   $K_n\subseteq\operatorname{int}K_{n+1}$ and $\bigcup_nK_n=U$, after discarding finitely many initial sets so that $(0,0)\in\operatorname{int}K_1$, its stopped
   pieces at $\tau_{K_n}$ are true martingales and
   $\tau_{K_n}\uparrow\tau_U$ almost surely. This is not a claim that
   $f(t,B_t)$ is defined after the lifetime or that these times tend to infinity.
items.strategy: Normalize Brownian null paths under usual conditions; smooth a continuous cutoff in an ambient extension neighbourhood. Prove distance-based exit measurability and compact exhaustion. Strict-lifetime predictable indicator is a union of stopped intervals; apply finite-energy dominated convergence and identify limits on increasing pre-exit events.

items.title: Heat-semigroup martingales
items.statement: Assume AC. For bounded Borel g and fixed T, P_{T-t}g(B_t), extended at T by g(B_T), is a bounded martingale. For t<T, u(t,x)=P_{T-t}g(x) is smooth and solves u_t+(1/2)Delta u=0.
items.strategy: Markov gives M_t=E[g(B_T)|F_t], so tower proves the martingale. Differentiate the positive-time Gaussian convolution under the integral using Gaussian derivative bounds and the heat-kernel equation.

items.title: Characteristic exponential for a continuous local martingale with deterministic clock
items.statement: Assume AC. For a real continuous local martingale M with M_0=0 almost surely on an arbitrary filtration and deterministic-partition quadratic variation [M]_t=t, the increment conditional characteristic function is exp(-theta^2(t-s)/2) and exp(i theta M_t+theta^2t/2) is a complex martingale.
items.strategy: Normalize on one measurable null set in an explicitly enlarged filtration and descend event tests at the end. Prove continuous stopping through finite-grid sampling and terminal conditional-expectation uniform integrability. Use the original localizers to justify bounded level stops. Prove the stopped partition clock, weighted convergence with ordered limits, L2 bounds on square sums, Taylor remainder L1 convergence, and telescope on [s,t].

items.title: Levy characterization of Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. A real continuous local martingale M with M_0=0 and [M]_t=t on a usual filtered space is Brownian motion with respect to that filtration.
items.strategy: Use the preceding characteristic-exponential martingale and divide its conditional identity at t by its F_s-measurable value to get the conditional characteristic function of M_t-M_s. Uniqueness gives N(0,t-s) independent of F_s; iterate for independent increments, then use continuity.

items.title: Vector Levy characterization
items.statement: Assume AC. If continuous local M=(M^1,...,M^d) starts at zero and [M^i,M^j]_t=delta_ij t, then M is standard d-dimensional Brownian motion.
items.strategy: Use the scalar characteristic exponential coordinatewise and one-dimensional finite-measure Fourier uniqueness to obtain integrable zero-mean increments and true coordinate martingales. Finite linear combinations are then true martingales. Exact finite partition algebra gives their clocks. Apply the characteristic exponential componentwise, then multivariate finite-measure Fourier uniqueness on each earlier event, and induct on increment lists.

items.title: The Brownian differential generator
items.statement: Assume AC. For f in C^2(R^d), write Lf=(1/2)Delta f for the Brownian Ito differential operator. This does not assert that every C^2 function lies in the closed-operator domain of the Brownian semigroup generator on C_0(R^d).
items.strategy: Define the differential expression pointwise; identify its coefficients algebraically. Stochastic applications require their full hypotheses, explicitly including (H).

items.title: Dynkin formula for bounded Brownian stopping
items.statement: Assume AC and the explicit vector Brownian filtration hypothesis. For a bounded stopping time tau and real C_c^2 function f, normalized continuous path evaluation on the original space gives E f(x+B_tau)=f(x)+E integral_0^tau (Delta f/2)(x+B_s) ds.
items.strategy: Direct finite-grid stopped Taylor telescoping. Independent vector increments cancel the linear terms and evaluate the Hessian terms. Uniform Hessian continuity and fourth moments make total remainder o(1). Bounded f and Lf pass limits through expectations. No general Ito or shifted-law event interface.

items.title: Ito versus Stratonovich boundary
items.statement: Assume AC. This block uses left-endpoint Ito integration. Symmetric Stratonovich sums and their conversion rule are not defined here and belong to later stochastic calculus.
items.strategy: Distinguish elementary left-time measurable coefficients, the global L2 extension, and localization. Prove the finite symmetric-minus-left sum identity termwise; assert no convergence or Hessian-only conversion for arbitrary predictable coefficients.

items.title: General semimartingale calculus is outside this block
items.statement: The stochastic integration and Ito formulas are scoped to Brownian-driven processes, while the partition definitions accept broader continuous inputs conditionally on existence of the specified limits. General semimartingale integration and the enumerated further theories remain outside this block.
items.strategy: Record the precise scope boundary so Brownian formulas are not misread as general definitions or theorems.

items.title: A closed L2 subspace with trivial orthogonal complement fills L2
items.statement: Assume AC. If V is a closed linear subspace of real or complex L2(mu) and V perpendicular={0}, then V=L2(mu).
items.strategy: Under AC use the real/complex Hilbert pairing, derive parallelogram by expansion, choose a positive-index minimizing sequence and obtain a nearest point by completeness and closedness. Real and imaginary perturbations force orthogonality. Zero Hilbert space does not imply zero measure.

items.title: Brownian-filtration martingale representation
items.statement: Assume AC. In the usual augmented natural filtration of one-dimensional Brownian motion, every cadlag local martingale M equals M_0+integral H dB up to indistinguishability for a unique predictable locally square-integrable H modulo dt tensor P on localized horizons.
items.strategy: First remove the raw right germ by independent product density, Levy downward convergence, Blumenthal and L2 contraction; this establishes the Brownian increment interface for the usual filtration before integration is used. Characteristic step exponentials, Fourier uniqueness and pi-lambda show trivial mean-zero orthogonal complement. Apply the closed-subspace lemma to R_T plus constants in full real L2. Terminal truncations and Doob L1 on grids including the terminal endpoint establish continuity before level stopping. Prove bounded continuous stopping by grid optional sampling and fixed-terminal uniform integrability. Represent bounded pieces; use finite-energy isometry, independent combined-energy uniqueness and Tonelli on countable overlaps to patch twice. No general semimartingale representation is used.

items.title: Square-integrable Brownian terminal variables have Ito representations
items.statement: Assume AC. For X in L2(F_T) in the usual Brownian filtration, X=E[X]+integral_0^T H_sdB_s for a unique predictable H in L2(dt tensor P).
items.strategy: Invoke directly the fixed-horizon closed-range surjectivity R_T=mean-zero L2(F_T) established as the first stage of the preceding representation proof, applied to X-E[X]. Terminal Ito isometry gives uniqueness. This avoids assuming a cadlag or continuous regularization for the process E[X|F_t] before representation supplies one.

items.title: Brownian-filtration local martingales have continuous versions
items.statement: Assume AC. Every cadlag local martingale in the usual augmented natural Brownian filtration has a continuous version, unique up to indistinguishability.
items.strategy: Representation identifies it with a continuous localized Ito integral. Continuous versions agreeing at each time agree on rationals on one full-probability event, hence everywhere.

items.title: Ito formula for Brownian powers
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). Brownian power identity for n>=2, with explicit predictable integrand and normalized Lebesgue-path representatives, at all times on one full event. Square and cubic polynomial processes are continuous square-integrable martingales.
items.strategy: Finite binomial telescope: L2 step-integral convergence, orthogonal centered weighted squared increments, L1 vanishing higher powers and pathwise Riemann sums. Rational continuity gives process equality. Deterministic-time product telescope supplies cubic martingale integral.

items.title: Logarithm of geometric Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC and (H), with usual filtration conditions. Normalize B on an F_0-null event to an everywhere-continuous adapted zero-start Bhat. For x>0, define X_t=x exp((mu-sigma^2/2)t+sigma Bhat_t). Then X is a positive continuous Brownian Ito process with drift mu X and diffusion sigma X, and log X has drift mu-sigma^2/2 and diffusion sigma.
items.strategy: Apply Ito to the smooth global exponential along Bhat. Continuous adaptation proves predictability/progressivity and explicit finite-horizon exponential bounds prove local coefficient integrability. Take the ordinary logarithm of the defining exponential; no logarithmic localization or SDE existence theorem is used.

items.title: Exponential martingale Brownian tail bound
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). For a,T>0 the supremum of the normalized continuous Brownian representative satisfies P(M_T>=a)<=exp(-a^2/(2T)).
items.strategy: Finite dyadic first-crossing index, discrete optional sampling of the Gaussian exponential martingale, increasing strict grid exceedance events, then b increases to a and theta=b/T. No continuous hitting time or exit law.

items.title: Harmonic functions of planar Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). For planar Brownian motion on its usual augmented natural filtration, normalized everywhere continuous and zero-start, B_t^1 B_t^2 and (B_t^1)^2-(B_t^2)^2 are continuous local martingales. Stopping at any origin-centred disc of radius R>0 gives true square-integrable martingales.
items.strategy: Both polynomials are harmonic on the whole plane. Apply the compact space-time theorem to K_n=[0,n] times the closed radius-R disc, whose exit is n wedge tau_R. For each finite horizon choose n larger than it, identifying the disc-stopped identities and martingales. Gradient norms are bounded by R and 2R; integer radii exhaust all finite path segments.

items.title: Expected exit time from an interval
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). For a,b>0 and x in (-a,b), let B^x be the continuous canonical coordinate process under P_x with its usual augmented natural filtration and tau its first exit from (-a,b). Then E_x tau=(x+a)(b-x), hence E_0 tau=ab.
items.strategy: A rational-distance test on compact time intervals proves the literal exit is a stopping time. Multiply u(y)=(y+a)(b-y) by the explicit smooth chi_R for R>max(a,b); this agrees near the closed interval. Apply bounded Dynkin to tau wedge n, using normalized evaluations agreeing on the common full initial-value event. Finite endpoint exit gives the bounded-convergence limit zero; MCT identifies E tau without presupposing its integrability.

items.title: Hitting probabilities from an exponential martingale
items.statement: Assume AC and (H). On continuous canonical path space under shifted law P_x, equip Z with its usual augmented natural filtration and set X_t=Z_t+mu t, a,b>0, x in (-a,b). The upper-exit probability is (1-exp(-2mu(x+a)))/(1-exp(-2mu(a+b))) for nonzero mu, and (x+a)/(a+b) for zero mu.
items.strategy: For nonzero mu, exp(-2mu X_t) is a constant multiple of an exponential Brownian martingale. The LIL makes the drifted path tend in the sign of mu, so the continuous path exits in finite time. For C=(-infinity,-a] union [b,infinity) and tau=inf{t>=0:X_t in C}, continuity gives {tau<=t}=intersection_{m>=1} union_{q in Q intersection [0,t]}{dist(X_q,C)<1/m}: a hit implies the rational approximations, while on the compact interval [0,t] the reverse inclusion makes the continuous distance function attain its zero infimum. Since X is adapted, every event on the right lies in F_t, so the stopping-time definition applies directly without the Brownian-specific closed-hit lemma. Stop at tau wedge n; endpoint bounds give uniform integrability and dominated convergence, then solve the two-point expectation. For mu=0 invoke the earlier two-sided Brownian exit theorem directly (equivalently take the displayed continuous limit). For each bounded horizon, upward finite-grid rounding is justified by optional sampling and UI of conditional expectations of the fixed M_T; only exact stopped values have the almost-sure endpoint bound K. Infinite-exit evaluation is explicitly extended on its null event.

items.title: The ordinary chain rule fails for Brownian motion
items.statement: Assume AC. The rule d(B_t^2)=2B_tdB_t is false: B_t^2=2 integral_0^t B_sdB_s+t, and expectations distinguish the formulas for every t>0.
items.strategy: Use the square identity. The Ito integral has mean zero while E B_t^2=t, so omitting the quadratic-variation correction contradicts expectations.

items.title: An unbounded stopped exponential martingale needs uniform integrability
items.statement: Assume AC. Let Z_t=exp(B_t-t/2) and tau=inf{t:Z_t=1/2}. Then tau is finite almost surely and E Z_{t wedge tau}=1 for finite t, but Z_{t wedge tau} tends almost surely to 1/2. Thus the stopped family is not uniformly integrable and optional stopping at unbounded tau fails without UI.
items.strategy: Assume AC and (H), normalize to an everywhere-continuous zero-start realization before its filtration. Gaussian conditioning gives mean-one Z and EZ_t^2=e^t. LIL and IVT give finite level hit; exact rational contacts and compactness prove stopping, with countable choices covered by AC. Nested-grid Doob and MCT give L2 supremum control; bounded discrete sampling and DCT give mean one at t wedge tau. Integer-time UI convergence would force mean 1/2, a contradiction.
